title: Best Dragon Alternatives for Mac (2026)
summary: The best Dragon dictation alternatives for Mac in 2026, compared honestly on accuracy, custom vocabulary, hands-free control, price, and privacy.
body_markdown:
If you came here because Dragon no longer works the way it used to on your Mac, you are not imagining it. Nuance discontinued Dragon Professional Individual for Mac back in October 2018, and it never came back. Version 6 was the last one, so a perpetual license still opens, but there have been no updates in years, and the current Dragon Professional v16 line is Windows only. Dragon Home, the consumer edition, was retired in 2023. On a Mac in 2026, you are running unsupported software or nothing at all.


**The short answer:** the best Dragon alternatives for Mac in 2026 are Aqua Voice (fast, accurate dictation with a custom dictionary), macOS Voice Control (free, built in, for hands-free control), Talon Voice (power-user accessibility and coding), Superwhisper (fully offline), and Wispr Flow (polished cloud dictation). Which one is right depends on which half of Dragon you actually miss.


## The split nobody tells you about


Dragon did two very different jobs, and most "Dragon alternative" lists blur them together. Getting the split right is the whole decision.


- **Dictation.** Turning speech into accurate text, fast, with a custom vocabulary so it spells your names, terms, and jargon correctly. This is what most people used Dragon for day to day.
- **Hands-free control.** Running the whole machine by voice: moving the cursor, clicking, selecting, editing, and formatting without touching the keyboard or mouse. This is what made Dragon essential for people with RSI, limited mobility, or other accessibility needs.


If you mostly miss the dictation half, a modern dictation app will beat Dragon on accuracy and cost. If you need the control half, the right answer is a dedicated voice-control system, not a dictation app. The list below is organized around that, so match your pick to the job you actually need done.


## 1. Aqua Voice, best for fast, accurate dictation


We build Aqua Voice, so read this section as informed rather than neutral, and check the verifiable claims for yourself.


Aqua is the closest replacement for the part of Dragon most people used every day: dictate into any app and get clean, accurate text at your cursor. It runs on our own proprietary model,[Avalon](https://aquavoice.com/avalon-api) , rather than a shared off-the-shelf engine. At its debut on the OpenASR leaderboard in October 2025, Avalon ranked as the top proprietary model (it now sits sixth overall as newer open models have landed). On the AISpeak benchmark Aqua reports 97.3% accuracy, a self-reported figure, so weigh it as one data point. For an independent read, 9to5Mac ran the same passage through Apple Dictation and Aqua and counted 17 errors versus 1.


Two things matter for Dragon refugees specifically. First, a **custom dictionary** : the reason people trained Dragon was to nail proper nouns and specialist terms, and Aqua lets you add your own so it stops mangling them. Second, **Voice Edit Mode** : you can revise text by voice ("change 'meeting' to 'deadline'", "delete the last sentence") without reaching for the keyboard, which recovers a slice of the hands-free feel Dragon users are used to. Final text lands in about 450ms, and you can dictate up to 230 words per minute.


- **Platforms:** Mac (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows, iPhone.
- **Languages:** 49.
- **Price:** Free for 1,000 words as a lifetime allowance (not a timed trial), then Pro at $8/mo billed annually.
- **The honest tradeoff:** Aqua is a dictation tool, not a full hands-free control system, and it processes speech in the cloud. If you need to run your entire Mac by voice, or you require fully local processing, see the picks below. If you want the direct comparison, we keep a running[Aqua Voice vs Dragon](https://aquavoice.com/vs/dragon) page.


## 2. macOS Voice Control, best free hands-free control


This is the pick that surprises people, because it is already on your Mac. Voice Control is Apple's accessibility feature (System Settings, Accessibility, Voice Control), and it is a genuinely different thing from the basic Dictation that types when you tap the mic. Voice Control lets you navigate, click, select, scroll, and edit by voice, with number and grid overlays for reaching anything on screen, plus dictation on top. For the hands-free-control half of Dragon, it is the best free starting point on macOS.


- **Platforms:** Mac (built in), also on iPhone and iPad.
- **Price:** free.
- **The honest tradeoff:** the command grammar is shallower than Dragon's decade of refinement, the dictation engine underneath is basic rather than Dragon-grade, and there is no deep custom-vocabulary training. It covers the control need well and the accuracy need only adequately, which is exactly why pairing it with a stronger dictation app is common.


## 3. Talon Voice, best for power users and coding


If your reason for using Dragon was serious hands-free operation, RSI, limited mobility, or writing code without a keyboard, Talon Voice is the tool the accessibility community actually reaches for. It is on-device, cross-platform, and cleanly separates a command mode (short spoken phrases trigger precise actions) from a dictation mode. People run their entire development workflow through it.


- **Platforms:** Mac, Windows, Linux.
- **Price:** a free public version, with the newest builds behind a low-cost Patreon.
- **The honest tradeoff:** Talon is a control framework, not a polished consumer app. There is a real learning curve, and you often build or install command sets to fit your work. The payoff is a ceiling nothing else here reaches for hands-free control, which is why it earns the spot despite the setup.


## 4. Superwhisper, best fully offline option


If part of what you liked about Dragon was that it ran on your own machine, Superwhisper is the closest match in spirit. It runs local speech models (including open Whisper builds it lets you choose) so dictation works on a plane, in a locked-down environment, or anywhere you would rather nothing leave the device. It also supports custom "modes" that reshape output for different contexts.


- **Platforms:** Mac, Windows, iOS.
- **Price at the time of writing:** around $8.49/mo, or a one-time lifetime license near $250.
- **The honest tradeoff:** local accuracy and speed depend on the model you load and the machine you run it on, so results vary more than a tuned cloud service, and setup asks a little more of you. It is dictation, not full hands-free control.


## 5. Wispr Flow, best polished cloud dictation


Wispr Flow is a well-made cross-platform dictation layer that cleans up your speech as you go and drops it into any app. If you want the smoothest install-and-talk experience and do not need offline processing, it is a strong option.


- **Platforms:** Mac, Windows, iPhone.
- **Price at the time of writing:** roughly $12 to $15 per month depending on billing, with a capped free tier.
- **The honest tradeoff:** it processes speech in the cloud, it is one of the pricier options in this category, and, like the other dictation apps here, it does not replace Dragon's hands-free control. Wispr does not publicly disclose the speech model behind it, so we do not attribute one. For the direct comparison, see[Aqua Voice vs Wispr Flow](https://aquavoice.com/vs/wispr-flow) .


## Two honest asides


**The free fallback: Apple Dictation.** Every Mac includes basic Dictation (press the mic key and talk). It is free and fine for a quick sentence, but it transcribes word for word and stops there, with none of the custom vocabulary, editing commands, or accuracy that sent people to Dragon in the first place. It is the 17-errors side of that 9to5Mac test, worth knowing as the zero-cost baseline. Our[Aqua Voice vs Mac Dictation](https://aquavoice.com/vs/mac-dictation) page has the detail.


**If you truly need Dragon itself.** For a narrow group, mostly legal and medical professionals who depend on Dragon's specific vocabularies and voice macros, no Mac app is a drop-in replacement. Dragon Professional still ships on Windows (around $699), so running it in a Windows virtual machine (Parallels or similar) on Apple Silicon is the honest path if that exact workflow is non-negotiable. For most people, that is more friction than it is worth.


## How to choose in one minute


- **You mostly want accurate dictation with your own vocabulary:** Aqua Voice.
- **You need to run your Mac hands-free and want it free:** macOS Voice Control.
- **You need serious hands-free control for RSI, accessibility, or coding:** Talon Voice.
- **Your hard requirement is that audio never leaves your device:** Superwhisper.
- **You want the smoothest cloud dictation and price is secondary:** Wispr Flow.


Dragon set a high bar, and the honest truth is that no single Mac app rebuilds all of it. But the dictation half, the part most people actually used, is better in 2026 than it was on Dragon: more accurate, cheaper, and available in every app without a training session. New to voice input? Our[setup guide](https://aquavoice.com/guide) walks through getting comfortable, and you can[try Aqua free](https://aquavoice.com/) on your next email before you decide.


## FAQ


**Is there a Dragon NaturallySpeaking version for Mac in 2026?**


No. Nuance discontinued Dragon Professional Individual for Mac in October 2018 and never released a replacement. Existing version 6 licenses still run but receive no updates, and the current Dragon Professional v16 is Windows only. For Mac, you need an alternative.


**What is the closest thing to Dragon for accurate dictation on a Mac?**


For the dictation half of Dragon, Aqua Voice is the closest match: high accuracy from its own Avalon model, a custom dictionary for your names and terms, and text you can edit by voice, across every app. It is $8/mo billed annually with 1,000 words free to start.


**What can I use for hands-free control like Dragon on a Mac?**


macOS Voice Control, built into every Mac for free, handles navigation, clicking, and editing by voice and is the best free starting point. For heavier accessibility or coding needs, Talon Voice goes further, at the cost of a steeper setup.


**Is there a free Dragon alternative for Mac?**


Yes. macOS Voice Control and Apple Dictation are both built in and free, Talon Voice has a free public version, and Aqua Voice includes 1,000 words free as a lifetime allowance before its paid tier.
